mcat_description.short: A mini greenhouse is a small prefabricated or semi-permanent enclosed structure with a transparent polycarbonate, polyfilm, or UV-stabilised plastic covering over a metal (GI/MS) or PVC frame, designed to create a controlled growing environment for plants. Sold as a complete kit or assembled unit, it is used for home gardening, terrace farming, nursery propagation, and small-scale protected horticulture.
mcat_description.long: Mini greenhouses are compact, prefabricated plant-growing enclosures that use a transparent or translucent covering material — most commonly twin-wall polycarbonate panels or UV-stabilised polyethylene film — stretched over a galvanised iron, mild steel, or PVC pipe frame to regulate temperature, humidity, and light for optimal plant growth. In the Indian market, they range from small tabletop or shelf-type units for indoor/balcony use to walk-in structures typically spanning 6×6 ft to 20×30 ft, with the walk-in polycarbonate or polyfilm type being the dominant commercial form sold on B2B platforms. Key functional features include natural or fan-assisted ventilation, UV-resistant covering, sliding or zippered doors, and easy bolt-together assembly without specialised tools. Buyers include home gardeners, terrace farmers, plant nurseries, agri-entrepreneurs, and educational institutions seeking year-round crop protection from weather, pests, and temperature extremes.

market_context: In the Indian market, 'mini greenhouse' refers to a small prefabricated or portable enclosed growing structure, distinct from large commercial polyhouses (typically 1,000–4,000 sq m) that dominate the agricultural greenhouse sector. The dominant covering materials in India are plastic films (polyethylene, UV-stabilised) and polycarbonate panels — plastic holds the largest market share (>40%) while polycarbonate is the fastest-growing segment due to superior durability and UV resistance. Frame materials are predominantly galvanised iron (GI) pipe or mild steel (MS), with PVC used for lighter portable units. The Indian market distinguishes between: (a) functional walk-in mini greenhouses for home gardening, terrace farming, and nursery propagation — the primary B2B segment on IndiaMART; (b) decorative glass-and-iron terrarium-style mini greenhouses sold as home décor items — a secondary segment with different buyer intent. Key manufacturing hubs include Noida/Greater Noida (UP), Pune/Talegaon (Maharashtra), Ambala (Haryana), and Bhilai (Chhattisgarh). Government schemes (National Horticulture Mission, MIDH) subsidise polyhouse construction, driving demand from small farmers. Buyers evaluate on frame material (GI vs. MS vs. PVC), covering type (polycarbonate vs. polyfilm), ventilation system (natural vs. fan-pad), UV protection rating, ease of assembly, and overall dimensions.
